statement: For unrestricted generic complementary affine sections of SO(n,C), n≥2, the geometric monodromy group is S_D, where D is the matrix-entry degree of SO(n,C).

answer.text: For unrestricted generic complementary affine sections of SO(n,C), n≥2, the geometric monodromy group is S_D, where D is the matrix-entry degree of SO(n,C).
answer.display: S_D, D=deg SO(n,C) (the displayed degree formula).

source.location: Proposition 1.1 (PDF p.1); Remark 3.4 (PDF p.8); explicit Bertini reduction in caveats
source.version: arXiv:1809.07293v2 (24 October 2018). Proposition 1.1 and its proof apply in characteristic zero. The 2023 corrigendum concerns a characteristic-seven trinomial and does not affect this application.

notes:
This is an explicitly deduced consequence, not a claim that Kadets discusses this named variety. Take a general codimension dim(V)−1 linear section of the irreducible projective closure V. Bertini gives an integral curve C of degree D. Proposition 1.1 gives S_D as C meets a variable hyperplane; these loops are a subfamily of the unrestricted complementary-section problem, so the ambient monodromy contains S_D and equals S_D. For affine sections, a general complementary section misses the boundary V at infinity, which has dimension dim(V)−1; restricting the unramified base to this nonempty open preserves monodromy. This argument does not apply to fixed coordinate projections, physically constrained measurement subfamilies or reducible varieties. SO(n,C) is irreducible; arbitrary complementary cuts are essential. The n=1 problem is the trivial one-point case. Degree and connected reductive-group hypotheses: Brandt–Bruce–Brysiewicz–Krone–Robeva, arXiv:1701.03200v2, Theorem 1.1 and §2, https://arxiv.org/html/1701.03200v2 .

This is a catalogue application of the classical characteristic-zero sectional-monodromy theorem, called folklore in Kadets, Proposition 1.1. Kadets is cited for an explicit proof, not as the originator of that theorem; the stated Bertini reduction identifies the particular enumerative family.
scope: Unrestricted generic complementary affine linear sections of SO(n,C), n≥2, in its matrix-entry embedding; codimension n(n−1)/2.
